# cutover-fixtures.txt — labeled expected-match set for block-fragile-refs.sh detectors
#
# Per the reference-durability adversarial-review amendment (FMF-2 + CDF-2): the
# version-cutover detector is the single precision-sensitive class, and a warn-log
# is structurally blind to false NEGATIVES (a missed clause produces no log line).
# A checked-in fixture with a labeled expected-match set is the only mechanism that
# converts "tuned during shakedown" into a measurable gate. Flip-to-enforce is gated
# on this fixture passing.
#
# This file lives under core/hooks/testdata/ which is OUTSIDE the durable-corpus
# scope gate, so the hook does not fire on the fixture's own raw example content.
#
# FORMAT (one test case per non-comment line):
#   <EXPECT>\t<CLASS>\t<content to scan>
# where
#   <EXPECT>  = FLAG  (the detector MUST match this line)
#             | CLEAN (the detector MUST NOT match this line)
#   <CLASS>   = LINK | VERSION | ISSUEREF-OUT | ISSUEREF-IN | ISSUEREF-POS | URL | PATTERNDECL
#   <content> = the literal line content presented to the detector
#
# The ISSUEREF-POS class is a TRUE positional test (the -OUT/-IN classes fake block
# context with the class label; -POS carries the geometry explicitly). Its content
# column is itself a pipe-delimited triple — "<refline>|<lineno>|<line text>" — where
#   <refline> = the file line of the reference-block header (0 = no block in file)
#   <lineno>  = the file line of the scanned content
#   <line text> = the literal line presented to the shared positional classifier
# The runner splits the content column on the first two '|' and feeds (lineno, refline,
# line text) to core/hooks/lib/positional-issueref.awk — the same classifier the hook
# and CI call — so the suite tests the real classifier, not a re-encoding of it.
#
# The harness self-test (run-fixtures embedded in the hook's companion check) asserts
# every FLAG line matches its class detector and every CLEAN line does not.

# ─── Class L (markdown link) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
FLAG	LINK	See the spec at [the standard](core/standards/reference-durability-standard.md) for details.
FLAG	LINK	Pointer: [doc-link maintenance protocol](../standards/doc-link-maintenance-protocol.md).
CLEAN	LINK	State the rule unconditionally and summarize the referenced content inline.
CLEAN	LINK	The durability ladder rung 2 names a file by its content, not by a path link.

# ─── Class V (version-cutover apparatus) — the FMF-2 precision cases ─────────
# Real cutover apparatus (MUST flag). Includes the self-verification "v1.03 merge SHA"
# case and corpus-shape variants the broken spec regex missed (mid-line Cutover, EOL
# "merge SHA", slug-suffixed versions).
FLAG	VERSION	Cutover: applies to releases entering Stage 4 strictly AFTER v1.03 merge SHA
FLAG	VERSION	v1.03 merge SHA recorded in the release log
FLAG	VERSION	Append-pattern detection applies to releases entering Stage 4 strictly AFTER the v11.07b merge SHA.
FLAG	VERSION	the v11.07b release itself is exempt (reflexive-pipeline-loop discipline)
FLAG	VERSION	v1.01-intake itself is exempt — the rule cannot fire on its own bundling
FLAG	VERSION	**Cutover:** Applies to releases entering Stage 13 strictly AFTER v11.19 merge SHA
FLAG	VERSION	Events occurring on or after the first release strictly AFTER v11.07a merge SHA; v11.07a itself exempt
# Benign prose that names a version but is NOT cutover apparatus (MUST stay clean).
# These are the FMF-2 false-positive cases the fixed regex must not trip on.
CLEAN	VERSION	The release v2.0 shipped and v2.1 is now the current line.
CLEAN	VERSION	v2.1 is now current
CLEAN	VERSION	We support macOS v12.3 in production and the feature is exempt for admins someday.
CLEAN	VERSION	Our policy v3.0 covers everyone and nobody is exempt here at all.
CLEAN	VERSION	Acceptable in release notes as a narrative identifier; banned in governance rule text.
CLEAN	VERSION	A release-plan filename template names the version segment as a placeholder shape.

# ─── Positional issue-reference: OUTSIDE a reference block (MUST flag) ───────
# A bare issue reference in body prose, with no designated reference block present.
# Synthetic placeholder numbers (high range, no real tracked issue) — these are test
# data for the #N-shape detector, NOT references to any real issue.
FLAG	ISSUEREF-OUT	The dedupe rule was introduced to handle the migration edge case (provenance: #90001).
FLAG	ISSUEREF-OUT	This behavior traces back to the original triage decision in #90002.

# ─── Positional issue-reference: INSIDE a reference block, self-describing ───
# A bare issue reference inside a reference block, accompanied by a summary noun
# phrase (>= 3 non-reference words). MUST stay clean — this is the sanctioned form.
CLEAN	ISSUEREF-IN	Parent reference-durability issue establishes the standard and enforcement spine — #90001.
CLEAN	ISSUEREF-IN	Sister repository-integrity gate composes by position with this workflow — #90002.

# ─── Positional issue-reference: INSIDE a block but CONTENT-FREE (MUST flag) ─
# A bare issue reference with no accompanying summary — the rung-5 "summarize inline"
# violation that no other primitive enforces.
FLAG	ISSUEREF-IN	#90001
FLAG	ISSUEREF-IN	- #90002

# ─── Positional issue-ref: block present but BELOW the ref line (the #314 divergence) ─
# Synthetic placeholder numbers (high range; not real tracked issues). Refblock header at
# file line 50; the body ref sits at line 20 — ABOVE the block → must FLAG OUTSIDE-BLOCK.
# This is the exact case the position-blind CI passed and the position-aware hook caught:
# the CI's existence-only `hasblock != 0` check sees a block somewhere in the file and lets
# a self-describing body ref through, while the hook's `NR >= refline` flags it.
FLAG	ISSUEREF-POS	50|20|This traces back to the original triage decision in #90002.
# Same self-describing ref AFTER the block (line 60) → must stay CLEAN (sanctioned form).
CLEAN	ISSUEREF-POS	50|60|Parent issue establishes the standard and enforcement spine #90002.

# ─── Hex-color exclusion (#2068): #NNNNNN color prefixes are NOT issue refs ───
# The bug: ISSUEREF_RE's `#[0-9]+` greedily matched the numeric prefix of a hex color
# (#28A745 → #28) and flagged it as a bare issue ref. The fix masks hex-color spans (a hex
# run with >=1 hex letter, OR a colon-prefixed CSS `:#hexdigits` run) to spaces in the
# shared classifier BEFORE the issue-ref test. Rows:
# (1-2) the exact bug — a hex color outside a block must NOT flag; (3) letter-first + short-
# hand hex shapes (#0A0/#FFF); (4) regression guard — a real #N outside a block STILL flags;
# (5) mixed line — a hex color present but a real #N must still flag OUTSIDE-BLOCK; (6) in-
# block self-describing line WITH a hex color present stays CLEAN (hex not counted toward the
# 3-word self-describe threshold). Synthetic high-range issue numbers (not real refs).
CLEAN	ISSUEREF-POS	0|10|The palette success color is #28A745 in the grammar table.
CLEAN	ISSUEREF-POS	0|10|Palette: #28A745 success, #17A2B8 info, #6C757D muted.
CLEAN	ISSUEREF-POS	0|12|Shorthand hex #FFF and letter-first #0A0 are colors, not refs.
FLAG	ISSUEREF-POS	0|10|This traces to the decision in #90002 for context.
FLAG	ISSUEREF-POS	0|10|Palette #28A745 relates to the fix in #90002 here.
CLEAN	ISSUEREF-POS	5|10|Green #28A745 maps to the success state #90002 in the map.
# Pure-digit hex colors in CSS/Mermaid `color:#NNNNNN` context (the exact process-flow-diagram-
# standards.md classDef lines that regressed the allowlist removal). #155724 / #856404 have NO
# hex letter, so the letter-anywhere branch alone misses them — the colon-prefixed branch
# `:#<hexdigits>` masks them. Must stay CLEAN (they are colors, not refs).
CLEAN	ISSUEREF-POS	0|39|    classDef automated fill:#D4EDDA,stroke:#28A745,color:#155724;
CLEAN	ISSUEREF-POS	0|41|    classDef gate fill:#FFF3CD,stroke:#FFC107,color:#856404;
# Regression guard: a colon-abutted DECIMAL that is a real ref-shape but NOT CSS — refs are
# never written `word:#NN` in the corpus; a self-describing #N after prose still flags.
FLAG	ISSUEREF-POS	0|10|The fix for the palette bug lives in #90002 here now.

# ─── Regex character-class hex form (issue #4182): `#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}` is a PATTERN, not a ref ──
# Second instance of the #2068 false-positive class. A durable-corpus file that DOCUMENTS a hex
# verification command carries the regex character-class form. The char after `#` is `[`, so
# neither the letter-bearing branch nor the colon-prefixed branch fires, and ISSUEREF_RE reads
# the leading `#[0` as a bracketed ref (`#[42]` is itself a legal ref shape). The third mask
# branch covers it, gated on a well-formed hex RANGE (X-Y) between the brackets. Rows:
# (1) POSITIVE — the real readiness-map-template.md:59 shape; must now be CLEAN.
# (2) NEGATIVE — a genuine bare ref in the SAME table-cell position; must still FLAG. This pair
#     is the proof the widening is precise rather than permissive.
# (3) PRECISION GUARD — a BRACKETED ref, the shape closest to a character class and the one a
#     broad `#[...]` widening would swallow; it carries no X-Y range, so it must still FLAG.
# (4) MIXED — the class form AND a real ref on one line; masking is span-local, so it must FLAG.
# Synthetic high-range issue numbers (not real refs), per the convention above.
CLEAN	ISSUEREF-POS	0|59|| TH-1 | No literal hex outside the `<style>` block | `sed '/<style>/,/<\/style>/d' <file> \| grep -coE '#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}'` → `0` |
FLAG	ISSUEREF-POS	0|59|| TH-1 | No literal hex outside the `<style>` block | see #90002 for the rule |
FLAG	ISSUEREF-POS	0|59|| TH-1 | The bracketed ref #[90002] is a reference, not a character class |
FLAG	ISSUEREF-POS	0|59|| TH-1 | `grep -coE '#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}'` per #90002 | `0` |

# ─── Class U (raw github.com/.../{issues,pull,milestone} URL) ────────────────
# A raw GitHub issue/PR/milestone URL is durability-ladder rung-6 — it rots on any
# repository move/migration. The URL class asserts the regex's CONTENT-match precision
# only; the ledger-surface exemption (release/releases/*, top-level CHANGELOG.md) and the
# allow-url marker are PATH/file-level properties evaluated by the hook + CI scope gate,
# exercised at the hook/CI integration test, not by this content-level fixture. Synthetic
# placeholder numbers/owners — test data for the URL-shape detector, NOT real references.
# Positive (the regex MUST match — issues/pull/milestone with a 3rd path segment):
FLAG	URL	See https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/333 for context.
FLAG	URL	The fix landed in https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/682 last cycle.
FLAG	URL	Milestone tracker: github.com/owner/repo/milestone/3 holds the slice.
FLAG	URL	The Anthropic example github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/42 is rung-6 too.
# Negative (the regex MUST NOT match — bare repo URL has no 3rd path segment; a word that
# merely contains "pull"; an install URL):
CLEAN	URL	Clone the repo: github.com/owner/repo then run install.
CLEAN	URL	The install URL https://github.com/owner/repo is documentation-exempt.
CLEAN	URL	The pullrequest workflow guide at github.com/owner/repo/pulls-guide is fine.
CLEAN	URL	State the rule unconditionally and summarize the referenced content inline.

# ─── Class PATTERNDECL (re-declaration of a single-sourced detector constant) ─
# The seven detector constants are declared once, in core/hooks/lib/fragile-ref-patterns.sh,
# and sourced by the hook, this runner, and the reference-durability CI. Sourcing removes the
# ability for the copies to DIVERGE; it does not remove the ability for a future edit to paste
# a literal back into a consuming surface, which would silently restore a second source of
# truth. These cases are the committed arms for the detector that the runner's scan arm then
# applies to the three real surfaces.
# Positives cover all THREE declaration syntaxes that existed before single-sourcing — the
# hook's `readonly N=`, the runner's plain `N=`, and the CI's copy indented inside a YAML
# block scalar. A checker that parsed only one of these was the rejected alternative, so a
# fixture that tested only one would leave the widening unproven.
FLAG	PATTERNDECL	readonly ISSUEREF_RE='#\[?[0-9]+\]?'
FLAG	PATTERNDECL	MIN_SELFDESCRIBE_WORDS=3
FLAG	PATTERNDECL	          HEXCOLOR_RE='(:#[0-9A-Fa-f]{3,8})'
# Negatives are true near-misses: each NAMES the constants and DECLARES none, differing from
# the positives only in the property under test (a declaration anchored at line start). An
# unrelated line would pass vacuously and prove nothing about the detector's precision.
CLEAN	PATTERNDECL	  -v issuere="$ISSUEREF_RE" -v hexcolor="$HEXCOLOR_RE" \
CLEAN	PATTERNDECL	# MIN_SELFDESCRIBE_WORDS operationalizes the rung-5 summarize-inline rule.
